notes_for_editor: Most narrative rests on LighthouseFriends and the West Vancouver Historical Society site (secondary, not independently verified; Graham 1985 not read). Disagreements left in the text: Woodward/Wellwood tenures, Erwin end 1909 vs 1910, fog alarm 1888 vs 1889, national designation 1974 vs 1994. Erwin's table entry (1907 volume) matched by adjacency of name and station only. Fiscal-year labels for 1900/1902 follow the corpus labels; the 1907 volume (v42, 1907-08) is cited loosely. The Parks Canada DFHD pages did not return text, so the 1974 designation date rests on the Register's citation of HSMBC minutes. Grafton's earlier hire as assistant 1889 is from the Vancouver Archives/MemoryBC search snippet only; roster dates for his assistant years are approximate. Access: record says closed; no source read states tower access rules. The 1912 'Anderson as Chairman of the Lighthouse Board' on the society page was not used (FHBRO says Chief Engineer). Checker 2026-10-27: Erwin end year differs inside the society site (keeper list 1909, Erwin page 1910); now stated in the story. LighthouseFriends gives the park as 65 ha (185 acres is about 75 ha); story keeps 185 acres and notes the mismatch. Erwin's keeper-table entries (1907 volume p.148) are on one OCR line with his station, and the 1900 table shows Point Atkinson with 'October 5, 1880'; the dismissed Register 'minutes' are sources, not stated designation dates.
